newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia, Russia air deal due April - minister.
newsitem.headline: Latvia, Russia air deal due April - minister.

text.p: Latvia's transport authorities hope to have an aviation agreement with Russia signed in April, Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans said on Monday.

Flight rights have been an issue between the two countries due to the debts in Russia of the insolvent former Latvian carrier Latavio. Russia has refused to grant a second Latvian airline the right to fly into Moscow due to the unpaid debts.
Krishtopans said that he had great expectations from the work of Latvian-Russian joint intergovernmental commission.
"I have big hopes for the pace of the commission's work...An agreement on aviation is included in a 20 item agenda as number one for the next meeting.
"The signing could take place during the second half of April," he said.
Two Russian companies fly to Riga while only one Russian-Latvian joint venture, Riair, has permission to fly to Moscow.
Latvian carrier Air Baltic, part owned by Scandinavian Airlines, has been denied access to Russia.
The joint Latvian-Russian commission was set up to solve outstanding bilateral issues after Latvia regained its independence from the former Soviet Union.
When asked about Latavio's debts, Kristopans said that there had been almost no movement.
He said the Latvian Privatisation Agency had suggested a possible solution but that the Russian side had not yet looked at it.
